subject: Cross-border egress, jurisdiction mapping, and data segmentation — clarifications
body:
Message 1 (original inquiry)
From: Elena Romero <elena.romero@stratusbank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up — clarifications on cross-border egress and legal jurisdiction

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the RFP packet. We have a few follow-ups specific to cross-border egress controls and legal jurisdiction that are blockers for legal review. Can you confirm the following:

1) If a customer pins to EU-hosted model instances, can any inference logs, traces, or artifacts be replicated to US controllers (for analytics/backups) without explicit contractual consent?
2) What contractual commitments do you accept around limiting export of customer data or inference-derived artifacts to named geographies?
3) In the event of a hardware incident requiring cross-region failover, what is the sequence for customer notification and explicit opt-out?
4) Do you offer per-customer on-prem or VPC-only options that guarantee no cross-border metadata flow to Redwood corporate systems?

We appreciate concise, itemized answers because our InfoSec needs to include them in the vendor risk matrix.

Best,
Elena
Director, Vendor Risk Management
StratusBank

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Key asks: egress of inference artifacts, contractual export limits, failover notification, VPC/on-prem guarantees.

Can we get a draft reply by Monday EOD PST? I will send to Elena once we align.

Message 3 (draft technical/responses from Rishi)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up — clarifications on cross-border egress and legal jurisdiction

Neha/Laura/Vivek — draft answers below. I've tried to keep them short and contract-ready; legal please flag any wording issues.

1) Egress of logs/traces/artifacts for pinned EU-hosted instances: By default, customer inference inputs, outputs, and associated telemetry (request/response, sampling traces, error logs) remain in the customer's selected region (EU) and are processed on regionally-resident compute. We do not replicate inference payloads or full request/response logs to US controllers for analytics or backups without explicit contractual consent.

2) Contractual commitments on export: Redwood can accept a contractual clause that prohibits export of customer inference data and derived artifacts outside the contracted geography except for (a) emergency incident response with agreed process, (b) anonymized/aggregated telemetry used for product safety unless customer opts out. We propose a Data Residency Addendum (DRA) that names permitted geographies and allows us to commit to non-export for operational backups and snapshots.

3) Cross-region failover: Technical failovers are governed by our Failover Playbook: prefer intra-region capacity first; if we must fail over cross-region, the sequence is: (a) automated attempt to route to local spare capacity; (b) controlled shift to alternative zone within same geography; (c) controlled cross-geography failover only when local capacity is exhausted or for safety reasons. Customer notification: we initiate a standard notification via email + portal banner within 30 minutes of failover start and provide incident timeline and remediation steps. Contract language: customers may require an opt-out that disables automatic cross-region failover; in that case we provide a documented manual-failover flow and an SLA-exemption (no automatic fallback).

4) VPC/on-prem options: Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) can be provisioned such that telemetry ingestion endpoints and control-plane metadata are configured to remain within customer-managed networks. For fully air-gapped on-prem deployments, we can operate with zero egress to Redwood corporate systems; for VPC deployments we can offer optional outbound egress filters and contractually defined telemetry routing.

Attachments suggested: short DRA template + failover annex.

I left out specific timelines for data purging and backup retention — Laura, can you add the legal/retention wording?

-rishi
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Message 4 (legal clarifications from Laura)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up — clarifications on cross-border egress and legal jurisdiction

Thanks Rishi — suggestions and legal-polished phrasing below for inclusion in an RFP response or DRA. Please use exact phrasing for contracting: 

A) Residency and replication: "Redwood will process customer inference inputs, outputs, and operational logs within the geographic region(s) expressly selected by the customer and set forth in the applicable ordering document. Redwood will not transfer such data outside the selected region(s) for processing, storage, or analytics, except as expressly permitted in this Agreement or by written customer authorization."

B) Export exceptions (to be enumerated in the DRA): "Permitted exports include (i) transfer required by law or legal process, (ii) emergency incident response involving customer agreement or when necessary to preserve system integrity, and (iii) anonymized, aggregated telemetry used for Redwood product safety and improvement, provided such telemetry cannot reasonably be re-identified."

C) Failover and notification: "Redwood's default operational policy is to utilize in-region spare capacity prior to cross-region failover. Where cross-region failover occurs, Redwood will provide initial customer notification within thirty (30) minutes via email and the Redwood Console incident banner, and a full incident report within 72 hours. Customers may elect a 'No-Auto-Failover' option; if chosen, automatic cross-region failover is disabled and an SLA exception will apply. The No-Auto-Failover option is documented in the DRA and requires coordination for manual failover steps."

D) VPC/on-prem guarantees: "For on-prem deployments, Redwood can operate in an air-gapped mode where no telemetry or metadata is transmitted to Redwood corporate control plane. For VPC deployments, Redwood will implement egress controls and may require secure control-plane tunneling; contractual language will define permitted control-plane metadata and the circumstances in which it may be accessed by Redwood operations. A specific network and telemetry design will be appended to the order form."

E) Retention: "Redwood will retain customer request/response logs and related operational telemetry for a period defined in the ordering document (default 90 days). Extended retention terms are available by agreement. Customers may request deletion of retained logs; Redwood will delete data in accordance with the agreed schedule and provide certification of deletion upon request."

Let me know if we want to add a statement on subprocessor locations and subprocessors' contractual obligations.

-Laura
VP Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Message 5 (final reply to customer from Neha)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — clarifications on cross-border egress and legal jurisdiction

Hi Elena — thanks for the questions and for being specific. Attached are two short artifacts that should map directly into your vendor risk docs: a one-page Data Residency Addendum (DRA) template and a Failover & Egress Annex that outlines notification windows and No-Auto-Failover option.

Summary (contract-ready bullets):
- Default residency: inference payloads, request/response logs, and operational telemetry are processed and stored only in the region you select (e.g., EU) and are not replicated to the US without written consent.
- Export exceptions: transfers only for legal process, emergency incident response (with customer engagement), or anonymized/aggregated telemetry for product safety (opt-out available).
- Failover: we exhaust in-region capacity first; cross-region failover is our last resort. We will notify within 30 minutes, and provide a full report within 72 hours. Customers may choose No-Auto-Failover; this disables automatic cross-region fallback and carries a documented SLA exemption.
- Private/on-prem: on-prem air-gapped installs can be run with no egress to Redwood corporate systems; VPC deployments can be configured with strict egress filters and contractually-defined control-plane metadata.
- Retention: default 90-day operational log retention; custom retention terms available in the DRA.

Attachments: Redwood_Dataplane_Egress_and_Jurisdiction_Answers.pdf (DRA + annex, 2 pages), MAL-SLA-Routing-Annex.pdf (1 page).

If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the DRA language and any subprocessor concerns.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
